price.title: Load SMARD auction prices
price.input: Weekly quarter-hour JSON series from Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de, for the Germany–Luxembourg bidding zone. Values are in €/MWh.
price.operation: Parse delivery timestamps into UTC, check duplicates and retain negative prices. A price below zero is a market outcome, not a missing value.
price.output: Earlier eligible prices supply lag features and training labels. Delivery-day outcomes are joined separately for evaluation.

weather.title: Load ICON-EU weather forecasts
weather.input: Open-Meteo Previous Runs, explicit German Weather Service ICON-EU model: hourly temperature at 2 m, wind at 120 m and shortwave radiation at twelve locations.
weather.operation: Use the fixed previous_day2 forecast lead, documented as 48 hours. Keep temperature in °C, wind in km/h and radiation in W/m². These are forecast conditions, not realised weather.
weather.output: Geographical weather features provide information about weather-sensitive demand and renewable supply. They do not directly calculate generation.

demand.title: Load ENTSO-E demand forecasts
demand.input: ENTSO-E monthly file extracts of Germany country day-ahead total load, in MW at quarter-hour resolution.
demand.operation: Keep the Germany country series and its version timestamps. The input area is Germany; the target price area is Germany–Luxembourg. Preserve that distinction.
demand.output: A demand value for each eligible delivery quarter, or a missing value with an availability indicator.

load.title: Validate and freeze three input tables
load.input: Archived source responses and retrieval metadata.
load.operation: Validate units, resolution, keys and conflicting rows. Store three typed Parquet tables with a fixed checksum manifest. Publish the manifest last, so an incomplete S3 snapshot cannot load.
load.output: A versioned input snapshot. Local evaluation reads it without calling source providers again. Reproducibility alone does not establish historical availability.

select.title: Select inputs available by 11:00 Berlin
select.input: Versioned prices, weather and demand, with delivery, source update and retrieval times kept distinct.
select.operation: For each forecast day, use the preceding day’s 11:00 Berlin deadline. Demand selects the latest nonmissing archived revision updated by that cutoff. Price and weather eligibility retain their stated timing assumptions. A forecast valid tomorrow can be eligible today.
select.output: Only inputs eligible under the declared policy, with gaps and timing limitations visible. A later archived revision cannot reconstruct an earlier missing value.

features.title: Build one feature row per delivery quarter
features.input: Eligible price history, hourly forecast weather, quarter-hour demand and the local calendar.
features.operation: Price lags match the same local quarter 1, 2, 7 and 14 days earlier; daily summaries capture recent levels. Hourly weather is repeated across quarters. Radiation is shifted back an hour because its timestamp describes the preceding hour. Add calendar features and explicit missing-value flags.
features.output: One feature row per delivery quarter, in three comparisons: prices/calendar; prices/calendar plus weather; prices/calendar plus weather and demand. Future realised observations never fill gaps.

labels.title: Select prices known before the monthly fit
labels.input: Realised prices for delivery dates before the monthly fit.
labels.operation: Select label versions eligible at the fold’s first issue cutoff. Historical feature rows keep their original daily cutoffs; fitting later does not replace them with revised information.
labels.output: Past feature/price pairs for learning. These labels are distinct from the later outcomes used to score this fold.

train.title: Fit three models once each month
train.input: The same eligible historical examples for three fixed CatBoost feature sets.
train.operation: Boosting combines decision trees to reduce quantile loss. Each percentile penalises errors asymmetrically. Expand the eligible training history at each month boundary. Training features retain the information cutoff of 11:00 Berlin on the day preceding each historical delivery day.
train.output: Three fitted CatBoost models: prices/calendar, plus weather, plus weather and demand. Save them and reuse them for every forecast day in that month. Settings are fixed before evaluation.

predict.title: Predict five prices per quarter-hour
predict.input: Delivery-day features and the saved monthly models.
predict.operation: Evaluate the fitted trees to obtain five quantile outputs. Sort their values into increasing order when raw outputs cross. The reference averages yesterday/last-week same-clock prices, with documented missing-history fallbacks, then adds training-error offsets.
predict.output: The 2.5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 97.5th percentiles for each quarter. These describe marginal uncertainty, not a joint daily price path.

fallback.title: Choose a usable system forecast
fallback.input: Candidate model predictions, whole-source availability and execution status.
fallback.operation: Choose demand → weather → prices/calendar → reference as permitted by source availability and execution success. Partial gaps remain missing values. Never choose a model using the realised price or its score.
fallback.output: A selected system forecast and an explicit fallback reason, both retained in the evaluation.

truth.title: Join realised prices after prediction
truth.input: Realised SMARD auction prices for evaluated delivery quarters.
truth.operation: Join by UTC delivery timestamp after generating predictions. This preserves both repeated autumn clock quarters. Leave absent truth missing and exclude those rows from every comparison together.
truth.output: Matched forecast/outcome rows for evaluation, without feeding outcomes back into historical prediction.

score.title: Score every method on matching outcomes
score.input: All three feature-set forecasts (prices/calendar, plus weather, plus demand), the simple reference and the selected system forecast, paired with identical available realised prices.
score.operation: Measure median errors, band width and observed coverage. Weighted interval score balances narrow bands against penalties outside them. Aggregate by day, month and full period; use seven-day blocks for uncertainty in the full-period score difference.
score.output: Comparable results with sample counts and limitations. A lower score does not by itself establish reliable bands, live readiness or trading value.

reference.title: Calibrate the yesterday / last-week reference
reference.input: Earlier same-clock prices and training-period forecast errors, available before the monthly fit cutoff.
reference.operation: Average yesterday’s and last week’s price for the same local quarter. Use one if the other is absent; use an earlier same-quarter median if both are absent. Estimate five error offsets using training data only. Reuse that calibration during the month.
reference.output: A separate simple reference forecast with five quantiles per quarter. It is compared with all three trained models and is the final system fallback.

models.title: Reuse the saved monthly models
models.input: The three monthly fitted models and the separately calibrated reference.
models.operation: Load the same fitted models and reference calibration for each delivery day in the month. Daily features change; fitting and calibration do not use that month’s evaluation outcomes.
models.output: Fixed predictors ready to consume each day’s eligible feature rows.

output.title: Five price estimates for every quarter-hour tomorrow
output.input: Candidate forecasts and the automatic system selection.
output.operation: Retain the 2.5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 97.5th percentiles in €/MWh. The 50th is the median estimate; the 25th–75th form the central 50% band and the 2.5th–97.5th form the central 95% band. These nominal bands need measured coverage.
output.output: A next-day price curve and uncertainty bands: normally 96 quarters, or 92/100 on clock-change days. This viewer shows saved historical forecasts, not a live service. Each quarter’s uncertainty is separate; the bands are not joint daily scenarios.
